newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Australia race row sign of immaturity - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Australia race row sign of immaturity - analyst.

text.p: The race row in Australia triggered by outspoken independent legislator Pauline Hanson is a sign that the country has yet to mature as a nation, a leading Indonesian analyst said on Thursday.

Soedjati Djiwandono from the Centre for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) said in a response to a lecture earlier in the day by an Australian academic that Australia was still undergoing the process of nation building.

The lecture and response was part of an annual series sponsored by the University of Indonesia and the Australian government's own Australia-Indonesia Institute and was this year titled "Is Australia A Racist Society?".

"The fact that Australia is continuing to grapple with the problems of multi-nationalism (multiculturalism) is an indication that Australia has not yet established itself as a nation," Djiwandono said.

He said the current Australian government did not follow the inclusive U.S. concept of the "melting pot" as Prime Minister John Howard, elected in March 1996, and Hanson used an exclusive term -- mainstream -- to describe their views.
This meant that some groups were left out, he said.

Far-right legislator Hanson sparked an often heated debate and founded her own political party after she told parliament in her maiden speech that she believed Australia was in danger of being "swamped" by Asian immigrants.
She also called for cuts in aid to Australia's Aborigines.
"Australia is still in the process of nation building, especially while migrants keep flowing into the country and the question of its Aborigines remains unresolved," Djiwandono said.
Earlier, Professor Andrew Jakubowicz of the University of Technology Sydney blamed Howard for "starting the fire on which Hanson poured fuel."

"While Prime Minister Howard has condemned racism, he will not endorse multi-culturalism. While he apologises personally for the Aboriginal stolen children, he will not commit his government to compensation," Jakubowicz said in his lecture.

He said Howard, who blames his party's past election losses on the ethnic lobby, ended several key government multi-cultural bodies and policies after coming to office and implemented a 40 percent cut in funding for Aboriginal bodies.
